auditor_value: (c) F₂ could be smaller than, larger than, or equal to F₁ — both impulses have magnitude mv, but F = mv/t depends on the time each force acts, which is not given

findings.note: Wrong answer. Both forces have impulse of magnitude mv, so |F₁| = mv/t₁ and |F₂| = mv/t₂; with t₁ and t₂ unrelated, F₂ can be smaller, larger, or equal to F₁ (equal when t₂ = t₁). The correct option is (c), option 3. The solution's own steps 2 and 3 reason to exactly this and then print the opposite option.
findings.fix: "option": 3, "value": "F₂ could be smaller than, larger than, or equal to F₁"

findings.quote: F₂ ⋛ F₁, all three are possible = F₂ can never equal F₁
findings.note: A false, self-contradicting printed line: 'all three are possible' includes equality, and the same line then asserts equality is impossible. Equality holds whenever t₂ = t₁.
findings.fix: F₂ ⋛ F₁, all three are possible ⇒ option (c)

notes: Steps 1 and 2 and both common_mistakes entries (options 1 and 2) are correct; only the last line and the final answer are wrong. The solution takes F₁ and F₂ as constant (or average) forces, which is the standard reading.
